summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR) in India, including their purpose, calculation, and impact on central government employees and pensioners.

claims.claim: DA is a crucial component of salary and pension for central government employees and pensioners, designed to offset inflation's impact.
claims.note: Dearness Allowance is paid to government employees and pensioners as a cost of living adjustment to offset the impact of inflation.

claims.claim: Revisions to DA usually occur twice a year, in January and July, directly affecting take-home pay and pension.
claims.note: DA is reviewed and revised semi-annually, i.e. once every six months, based on the cost-of-living index. DA/DR is revised every six months w.e.f. July and January of every calendar year.

claims.claim: The allowance is fully taxable, meaning it is added to the employee's gross income before income tax calculations.
claims.note: Dearness Allowance is fully taxable. DA isn't a separate type of income – it's part of your salary package, and as per Indian tax rules, it's fully taxable for both salaried employees and pensioners.

claims.claim: The AICPI-IW is currently published with a base year of 2016=100, though the DA formula often references a previous base year (2001=100) through a linking factor for continuity.
claims.note: The Labour Bureau has changed the base year of the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers from 2001 to 2016. The new series of CPI-IW with base 2016 has replaced the existing series with base 2001. The linking factor for the new series (2016=100) to the old series (2001=100) is 2.88.

claims.claim: As per the 7th Pay Commission's recommendations, the formula for calculating the percentage of Dearness Allowance for Central Government employees is: DA % = ((Average of AICPI-IW (Base Year 2001=100) for the last 12 months – 261.4) / 261.4) * 100
claims.note: For Central Government Employees: DA% = [(Average of AICPI (Base Year 2001 = 100) for the last 12 months – 261.42)/261.42] x 100. The formula is DA% = [{12-month average of AICPI-IW (base year 2001)– 261.42}/261.42x100]. 261.42 is the AICPI-IW reading on 1 January 2016 when DA was reset to 0%.

claims.claim: 261.4: This is a fixed constant, representing the average AICPI-IW (Base Year 2001=100) as of January 1, 2016, which was the effective date for the 7th Pay Commission's recommendations.
claims.note: 261.42 is the AICPI-IW reading on 1 January 2016 when DA was reset to 0%.

claims.claim: For pensioners, Dearness Relief (DR) serves the same purpose, ensuring their fixed pension income retains its purchasing power.
claims.note: Dearness Relief (DR) is a cost-of-living adjustment paid to government pensioners and family pensioners in India. It is the pension-side counterpart of Dearness Allowance (DA), which is paid to serving employees.

article_title: Dearness Allowance: Understanding Your DA Hike Calculation Formula
